study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

answer: ABIDE structural MRI dataset (20 sites; cortical thickness; 569 controls, 482 autism)
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Public ABIDE multi-site structural MRI dataset with cortical thickness measures across 20 samples/17 sites; includes both typical controls and autism participants
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The ABIDE consortium ... provides a publicly available structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data set ... For this study, we used 569 controls ... In a subsequent step, we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set."

answer.ABIDE controls: normative model training/validation (age effects, site modelling)
answer.ABIDE autism: clinical evaluation set to test retention of clinically useful variance after site handling

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Controls split 70% train / 30% test within sites for hierarchical Bayesian models; autism sample used to evaluate clinical signal and prevalence of atypical z-scores after applying trained models
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we split the the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166)... Subsequently, we validate the hierarchical Bayesian models in the autism sample of the ABIDE data set"
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: study_2/Bayer2022.pdf.md: 3.3 Splitting the ABIDE data set
